mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions dampening corporate investment and consumer spending.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-trigger mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces consumer wealth and corporate hiring intentions.
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE > 4.5% for two months, the 60-day forward return is positive in at least 70% of instances (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds INDPRO by more than 10% for three consecutive months, it signals robust demand growth that precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) relative to the pre-trigger baseline in 40% or more of such events.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (index falling below 100) combined with a decline in HOUST (units of housing starts) by at least 15% in the same month predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing and housing activity signal supply-side stress.
failure_condition: Over 100 such triggered months, the 5-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of cases (frequency test).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of at least 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals persistent inflationary pressure eroding equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In inflationary regimes, the 20-day forward return is not negative in more than 60% of such episodes (frequency threshold).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment months) above 200,000 in a month, followed by a decline in UNRATE below 4%, predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market expansion supports economic momentum.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in 80% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) exceeds GDPC1 by more than 5% for two consecutive months, it indicates excess demand in retail, which precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in 50% of such triggers.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in UNRATE below 3.5% for four consecutive months in a non-recession regime is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as low labor costs reduce wage pressures and support corporate profits.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for 4 consecutive months AND not in recession regime
failure_condition: Over 100 such months, the 60-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of cases (frequency test).
